newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bildt to name supervisor for Bosnia town -sources.
newsitem.headline: Bildt to name supervisor for Bosnia town -sources.

text.p: Bosnia envoy Carl Bildt is expected at an international conference in Vienna on Friday to appoint a supervisor for the hotly disputed town of Brcko to help keep the Bosnian peace process on track, diplomats said.
"It is 99.9 percent certain it is going to be U.S. diplomat Robert Farrand," one diplomat said in Sarajevo.

"They're talking about the future of Brcko," an Austrian foreign ministry official said. "The tensions are high. They'll have to find some solution that safeguards the Brcko corridor but at the same time allows the people to live there."

U.S. arbiter Robert Owens three weeks ago ruled that the volatile town, claimed by both Serbs and the Moslem-Croat federation, would be put under international supervision pending a final decision next year on its status.

The river port town was captured by Bosnian Serbs early in the 1992-95 war and purged of its mainly Moslem-Croat pre-war population. Serbs had threatened to resume war if they were denied control of Brcko, which sits on a narrow land corridor linking eastern and western halves of Serb-controlled land.
The Moslems and Croats in turn claim Serb control over Brcko would reward so-called ethnic cleansing and deprive them of access to the Sava and Danube rivers and other main European waterways.

Washington's envoy to the Balkans, John Kornblum, has said the arbiter's decision to avoid a clear resolution of the issue was "definitely enough" to prevent renewed fighting between Bosnian Serb and Moslem forces.
The international community's High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt said the ruling had sought to strike a balance in "the mother of all difficulties in the Bosnian peace process".
Kornblum and Bildt, whose office will appoint the Brcko supervisor, will be heading the conference in Vienna's imperial Hofburg palace.

The supervisor would have the job of strengthening democratic institutions and overseeing implementation of the Dayton peace deal that ended Bosnia's war but was almost scuppered by the Brcko dispute.
The arbitrators also decided to name a supervisor to deputise for Carl Bildt.
Local newspapers in Sarajevo said Farrand is a career State Department diplomat with experience in eastern Europe.
If appointed, Farrand would be empowered to issue regulations to local police and to set up a multi-ethnic police force, according to the arbitration ruling.
The supervisor should also ensure full freedom of movement, oversee the return of Moslem and Croat refugees and implement an economic revitalisation programme for the Brcko area.
The Bosnian Serb delegation will be led by President Biljana Plavsic, while the Muslim-Croat federation's team was expected to be headed by President Kresimir Zubak.
Bosnia would be represented by Haris Silagelzic, Croatia by Foreign Minister Mate Granic and Yugoslavia by Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic, the Austrian foreign ministry said.
